claims.statement: The replay/acceptance drivers use a three-way exit code convention: exit 0 = gate passed, exit 1 = sanity/self-check failure (the 01_learn_* learners exit 1 when their S self-checks fail), exit 2 = gate not passed; because scripts run through conda run, a gate-FAIL (exit 2) makes conda print an ERROR line, which is a reporting convention not a crash — the output/ reports are the source of truth. Every gate driver returns `0 if passed else 2` from main().

The causal split (因果切分) is a hard invariant in Asia/Shanghai time that must not be broken: the learn window is frozen at 2026-04-14 to 2026-08-15 (DSS_LEARN_WIN_START/DSS_LEARN_WIN_END), replay windows use only later dates, and every prediction anchored at time t consumes only the per-car event with the largest timestamp <= t (rolling side via the T2 watermark line, static side via bisect lookups). The static side rebuilds the shared tmp_ev_base with a 7-day front margin (MARGIN_DAYS=7, >= longest journey 120h) so any car exiting inside the window has its entry event inside the extended window.

W1 acceptance (02_replay_eta.py) is a three-estimator offline replay (Σ段中位数 / Σ段均值 / 直接剩余分布) where the gate is the direct-remaining estimator: per-vehicle median |err| then cross-vehicle median <= 30min (GATE_SEC=1800s). The Σ estimators are hindsight path diagnostics only, not the production caliber.

W2 acceptance (02_replay_shift.py) D1' gate = plant-wide per-shift @5h median |err%| <= 10% AND each main model (per-shift actual median >= 30, MAIN_MODEL_MIN_MEDIAN) individually <= 10%; the count caliber (v3 re-anchor, 2026-09-21, revision 10) counts an in-progress car only if t + model_remaining <= window end, excluding stale ETAs (eta < anchor) from the shift.

M9 Step B (run_rolling) drives the production T2 pipeline unmodified in replay cursor time: bootstrap_hours=168 is injected via dataclasses.replace on the frozen DSSConfig so bootstrap and every 24h periodic rebuild use a 168h window matching the static 7d edge, the bootstrap is anchored at the replay start (not wall clock), each 5-minute step (STEP_SEC=300) calls the production run_one_round, and α observation uses pre-fetched exit events (one SQL, counted only within the observed window, no future leak). The alert_hook defaults to None (zero production impact).

The M9 Step A self-check requires the plant-wide 5h median |err%| to lie within SELF_CHECK_BAND, default (0.1089, 0.1339) — re-anchored in W4.4c (2026-10-06) from the old 8.74% anchor to the new-stack 11.63% static retest with band geometry (anchor −0.74pp / +1.76pp) preserved. Being out of band is a structural-drift declaration that stops the run with SystemExit (exit 2) to re-calibrate, and DSS_SELF_CHECK_BAND can override it with strict validation (malformed or out-of-range values raise ValueError rather than silently falling back).

M9 Step A runs a frozen local W2.1 replay script (default scratch/02_replay_kw37.py, overridable via DSS_M9_CROSS_MACHINE / DSS_M9_CROSS_DIR) as a subprocess for the fixed 09-05 to 09-13 scenario-2 window and compares 5h predictions per shift; |Δpred| > 2 台 (CROSS_MAX_DELTA) on any one shift, or a missing shift / no fresh CSV produced, raises SystemExit under the 单班超差停机规约 (single-shift over-diff stop rule) and prevents entry to Step B.

M9 gates() is a pure function judged per DSS_ALPHA_MODE: G1 (α=off engine consistency, unchanged in both modes) = per-shift |roll_off − static| <= min(p3_inproc,25)+2, p3 hard cap 25 (P3_CAP), and full-plant plus mid-shift 5h relative error difference <= 0.5pp (PP_TOL). With alpha_mode=off (production default) G2 = plant off 5h median <= 10%, G3 = True by definition, G4 = False by definition; with on, G2 = on <= 10%, G3 = on <= off, G4 = mid on < off. Overall pass = G1 ∧ G2 ∧ G3 ∧ (G4 ∨ g4_soft), where g4_soft requires G1–G3 met and DSS_G4_HARD != 1 (G4 软化: a failing G4 does not block when G1–G3 hold); DSS_G4_HARD=1 restores the hard gate and has production meaning only when DSS_ALPHA_MODE=on.

M10 (03_alert_backtest.py) reuses M9 run_rolling with an alert_hook that runs the production AlertEngine each 5-minute step (engine self-computes predictions from the pool to prevent M9 error propagation) and captures anchor snapshots; M10 alerts are emitted only as JSON/MD and never written to any dss table (2026-09-25 拍板⑤), and the backtest run is α=1.0 pinned.

The M10 gate set: G0 = the tests/test_w3_alert.py subprocess passes (returncode 0 and 'passed'); G1 = all-day main-view 21:30 anchor median |Δ5h − Δ终局| <= 5pp over all-day scope-days and zero all-day red at 21:30; G1b = engine 5h pred == M9 JSON pred_off@5h for every shift (14/14); G2 = 21 scope-day (14 shift + 7 all-day) level == grade(Δ) with the debouncer-lag exemption; G3 = every non-green final scope-day's first confirmed final-level alert (baseline included) arrives no later than the 3h anchor (lead time >= 2h); G4 = no confirmed transition inside the half-open [anchor−10min, anchor) window before the 5h anchor (2026-09-26 拍板 B; transition count downgraded to the observation item G4_obs); G5 = pool product cars = in-progress + bottleneck + no-ETA (exact) and pool n == M9 inproc_5h_n; G6 = all 21 scope-days covered by at least one alert. Overall pass = all eight gates.

M5 acceptance (04_m5_acceptance.py) primary criterion is per workday per shift-row 5h-anchor |Δ实际| <= tol (default 10%), where Δ实际 = (pred − 实际终局) / 实际终局. The 5h anchor is work_start+5h (day anchors follow shift type via DAY_TYPES: 11h→10:00 / 10h→11:00 / 8h→13:00; mid constant 21:30) matched by ±3min tolerance (ANCHOR_TOL_SEC=180); 实际终局 = the 4 offline-point (K3IS140 / 1J440RB / K2IS075 / K1IS135) product-car closed-interval count (day [D 04:45, D 16:30], mid [D 16:30, D+1 MID_END_TIMES[type]]), the same <= end closed-interval semantics as the predictor's a_of.

M5 rows are classified into four mutually exclusive reason buckets — gated (scored), actual_zero (actual final 0, out of gate), stale (anchor frame guard status STALE, out of gate), anchor_missing (no anchor frame within tolerance — an explicit recorded row, never silently skipped) — with priority stale > actual_zero > anchor_missing; the final verdict is PASS only if no gated row fails.

M5 STALE rounds are merged into consecutive spans (a gap > 5min breaks a span; each span's end is extended by one 5min round) and are not gated (ETL SLA 拍板). --snap-dir is repeatable with first-seen-wins on timestamp duplicates, and find_sibling_run_dirs explicitly WARNs about same-prefix -rN run directories that were not passed; the script is read-only with zero DB writes (SELECT only) and writes only local MD/JSON.

The gate discipline is gate-pure-function-first TDD: each gate (M9 gates(), M10 gate_g0..g6, M5 assess/anchor_for/pick_anchor/stale_stats/alert_ledger) is unit-tested on synthetic/offline data before the replay wiring exists. For example tests/test_w3_m9.py drives gates() on 14 synthetic shifts (off/on branch plus per-criterion flip cases) with no DB.

A failed gate is a legitimate measured result requiring attribution before any revision: the W1/W2 failure path requires locating the error source from the report's per-bucket diagnostics before a gate revision is proposed. Softening (e.g. the G4 soft disposition, or keeping DSS_SHIFT_TIER_DELAY=0 after the W4.4h experiment failed to improve G2) is only ever decided with data, back to the decision owner, and recorded; conversely a passed gate can still be closed with a historical FAIL number left on the record (不软化不删门).

The widely cited acceptance numbers — 14.16% (W2 v3 re-anchored plant-wide 5h median, window 08-16→09-19), 12.30% (W2.1 full-window 35-day baseline), 8.08% (good-week plant-wide with the shift calendar), and 11.26% (KW37 rolling off G2) — are historical baselines sourced from CHANGELOG.md/docs; the evidence details live in the output/ report filenames referenced by those entries (e.g. output/w2_replay_gate_*.json, output/w4-KW37-影子回放.md), whose contents are not reproduced in the wiki.

M9 and M10 share the replay window from DSS_M9_START / DSS_M9_END (defaults 2026-09-05T00:00 / 2026-09-13T23:59:59, Asia/Shanghai) and both read plan_inbox/week_plan_*.csv schedules with strict discipline — a missing in-window date raises KeyError (缺排班不得静默丢班) and conflicting rows across files raise ValueError. All shift geometry (work starts, attribution windows, MID_END_TIMES, the {3,4,5,6}h anchors and the 5h gate anchor) comes from the single source of truth spike_w2/shifts.py, which W3 code must not duplicate.
